We are a close-knit team, and we believe in serving customers rather than simply selling to them. You will  be the HR function, with no HR team under you, and you will keep the Partner's time, meetings and follow-ups organised. Expect roughly a 60:40 split between HR and executive support, varying week to week. As the business evolves, the scope of this role may change over time. We want someone who welcomes that. This role suits someone who enjoys doing the work personally, likes order and follow-through, and wants to see the direct impact of their work on a growing business. HR AND ADMINISTRATION •      Hiring:  Run recruitment end to end for roles such as sales engineers, accounts, stores/dispatch and office staff: job posts, screening, interviews, reference checks, offer and appointment letters. •      Joining and exits:  Joining documentation and induction. Handle exits with sensitivity and in line with labour law: notices, documentation, handovers and timely full-and-final settlements. •      Attendance and payroll:  Maintain attendance and leave records and share accurate monthly payroll inputs, advances, reimbursements and new-joiner/exit details with Accounts, who handle PF, ESI and other statutory filings. •      Policies and records:  Keep employee files complete and confidential. Draft and maintain a simple HR policy handbook covering leave, attendance, conduct and travel. •      Performance:  Help set KRAs for each role, run the review cycle on time, and flag training needs. •      People and culture:  Be the first point of contact for employee concerns, handle routine matters fairly, and escalate sensitive issues to the Founder. •      Office administration:  Oversee office upkeep, supplies, company assets and service vendors. EXECUTIVE ASSISTANCE TO THE FOUNDER •      Manage the Founder's calendar, meetings and reminders, and flag conflicts before they happen. •      Prepare agendas, take notes in internal meetings, and track every action item until it is closed. •      Draft professional emails, letters, presentations and reports when asked. •      Follow up with team members on agreed deadlines and send the Partner a short weekly status update. •      Coordinate customer and principal meetings, visitor arrangements, travel bookings and related documents. •      Maintain organised physical and digital filing of important documents. •      Handle business, financial and personnel information with complete discretion. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YOUR FIRST 6 MONTHS •      Every employee file and attendance record is complete and up to date. •      Every exit is handled respectfully, fully documented and closed without disputes. •      The team stays motivated and stable, and key people are retained. •      A written HR policy handbook is in place and shared with the team. •      The Partner's meetings, follow-ups and deadlines run without reminders. WHAT YOU MUST HAVE •      Graduate in any discipline. MBA or PGDM in HR is preferred. •      7 to 12 years of experience, including at least 5 years of  hands-on  HR operations: recruitment, attendance, documentation and payroll inputs. Experience in a small or mid-sized company (trading, manufacturing or industrial) is a strong plus. •      Has personally handled employee separations end to end, including difficult conversations, documentation and full-and-final settlements, with working knowledge of the labour law involved. •      Fluent Hindi and good written and spoken English. •      Working confidence in Excel (sorting, filters, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, basic pivots), Word, email and calendar tools. •      Based in Ranchi or relocating before joining, with a reliable daily commute. •      Punctuality, discretion, fairness and the habit of closing tasks without being chased. Good to have:  experience as an assistant to a promoter or MD, familiarity with an HRMS, payroll software or Tally, and exposure to B2B or industrial businesses. We are looking for a long-term association. •      You cannot join within 7 days. •      You are uncomfortable being the single point of accountability. There is no one below you to hand work to. We also run a punctual, gossip-free workplace where confidential information stays confidential. If that does not come naturally to you, this will not be a good fit. HOW TO APPLY Email your resume to  services@hehindia.in  with the subject line:  HR-EA | Your Name | Years of Experience In the body of the email, answer these five questions briefly: 1.    Which area of Ranchi do you live in? 2.   Your current and expected monthly in-hand salary. Attach current pay slip. 3.   Your notice period.  4.   In 3 to 5 lines, describe one HR process you personally set up or fixed, and what changed as a result. 5.    In 3 to 5 lines, tell us how you handled a day when your manager gave you two urgent tasks at once. Applications without answers to all five questions will not be reviewed.  Shortlisted candidates will hear from us within 7 working days. The process is a short phone call, a 30-minute practical task at our office (drafting an email and a simple Excel exercise), and a final conversation with the Partner.

review_candidates.description: Overview As a member of the military, General Surgeons belong to the Medical Specialist occupation in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) and provide trauma and general surgical care for CAF members, whether at a Canadian Forces Health Services Clinics/operating theatres or overseas in support of peacekeeping or humanitarian missions. They have the opportunity to be a leader within the CAF Health Services, as well as mentor and educator to other Health Services personnel, including Medical Officers, Nursing Officers, Physician Assistants as well as Medical, Operating Room and Diagnostic Technicians. Their primary responsibilities are to: Provide surgical consultation for Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) Members in Canada and deployed internationally; Lead a surgical or emergent care team caring for injured and ill patients in Canada and in deployed settings, internationally; Educate and advise multidisciplinary teams on trauma and general surgery care; Maintain a high level of surgical skills, by holding a position within a civilian health care facility ; and Contribute to the development and application of health care policies within the CAF. Work environment General Surgeons in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) maintain their clinical readiness by being embedded as staff in tertiary care civilian hospitals across Canada, working alongside their civilian colleagues. Part of their time may be spent providing consultative services to support Primary Care Clinicians at Canadian Forces Health Services Clinics in Canada. Participation in education and training tasks, as well as research opportunities, occur nationally and internationally. They belong to 1 Canadian Field Hospital and maintain their operational readiness by participating in annual military skills training and field exercises. When required, they will be called upon to deploy to unique and challenging clinical environments as part of a Health Services team on domestic and international operations. If you chose a career in the Regular Force, upon completion of all required training, you will be assigned to your first base. While there is some flexibility with regards to postings (relocations), accommodations can’t always be made, and therefore, you can likely expect to move at some point in your career. However, if you decide to join the Primary Reserve Force, you will do so through a specific Reserve unit. Outside of training, your chosen Reserve unit will be your workplace on a part time basis, and you will not be obligated to relocate to a different base. As part of the Primary Reserve Force, you typically work one night per week and some weekends as a minimum with possibilities of full-time employment. Entry plans Direct Entry Options If you are a member of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and have an unrestricted licence to practise in General Surgery in a Canadian province or territory, you may be eligible for enrolment and to commence basic training. Currently, the Canadian Armed Forces supports clinicians who practice in the following Surgical sub-specialties: Trauma Surgery Critical Care Medicine Vascular Surgery To find out more information or to apply to the CAF as a General Surgeon you can contact our recruiters at: HSRecruiting-RecrutementSS@forces.gc.ca Please indicate in the subject line of your e-mail: MEDICAL SPECIALIST Training At the first available opportunity, you will complete Basic Military Officer Qualification training at the Canadian Forces Leadership and Recruit School in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec. You will take the Condensed Health Services Basic Military Officer Qualification Training which consists of two weeks of Distance Learning and four weeks of in-house training in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu. Topics covered include general military knowledge, the principles of leadership, regulations and customs of the Forces, basic weapons handling, and first aid. Opportunities will also be provided to apply such newly acquired military skills in training exercises involving force protection, field training, navigation and leadership. A rigorous physical fitness program is also a vital part of basic training. Basic Military Officer Qualification training is provided in English or French and successful completion is a prerequisite for further training. Incoming Medical Specialists in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) will attend the Rank Qualification Medical Specialist Major (RQ-Med Spec-Maj) course delivered by the Canadian Forces Health Services Training Centre (CFHSTC). Consisting of an online asynchronous distributed learning (approximately 20 hours) and a five-day residential training phase, this course prepares Medical Specialists to provide expert care within the CAF health system and across operational environments. You will gain an understanding of key common CAF and Canadian Forces Health Services (CFHS) policies, CAF-specific and specialty-specific operational medicine, and the unique aspects of military healthcare. Upon completion, you will be equipped to deliver specialist healthcare in support of CAF members while leading multidisciplinary healthcare teams in both civilian and deployed settings. CAF General Surgeons may be eligible to apply for the opportunity to specialize their medical practice and, when applicable, can receive subsidy in exchange for additional years of service. Supported training will normally consist of a sub-specialty fellowship program at a Canadian University, but may include other Post-graduate degrees and/or courses determined to be complimentary to military practice. As they progress in their career, General Surgeons who demonstrate the required qualifications, ability and potential may be offered advanced training in the following areas: Forward Acute Care Resuscitation Team Training; Mobile Surgical Resuscitation Team Training; War Surgery Courses; Definitive Surgical Trauma Care Courses; Advanced Surgical Skills for Exposure in Trauma Courses; Medical Education and Simulation; and Military and health care leadership Part time options The role of the Canadian Forces Health Services Reserves is to provide trained personnel to support, augment and sustain Canadian Forces Health Services organizations for Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) operations and training activities, while building and maintaining links between the CAF and the local community. The role of the Canadian Forces Health Services Reserves is to provide trained personnel to support, augment and sustain Canadian Forces Health Services organizations for Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) operations and training activities, while building and maintaining links between the CAF and the local community. Members of this Primary Reserve unit complete a minimum annual commitment of 14 days of service and/or training at any time during the year, doing any or all of the following: providing health care services to Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) members, teaching and monitoring clinical skills of personnel, attending field exercises to practice and/or provide medical care in a military field environment. Medical Specialists serving in the Primary Reserve may live and work across Canada, as long as they are within a 100 km of a CAF Health Services unit. There is a small headquarters and administration section located in Ottawa, Ontario to assist them. All members of the Canadian Forces Health Services Reserves may have an opportunity to work internationally as members of a deployed Canadian Forces Health Services Team. Part-time opportunities within the CAF may exist for specialties and sub-specialties, depending on the requirements and position availability. These include: Anesthesiology Emergency Medicine General Surgery Internal Medicine (General, Infectious Diseases, Critical Care) Orthopedic Surgery Radiology Neurosurgery Plastic Surgery Thoracic Surgery Obstetrics and Gynecology Pediatrics Otolaryngology Urology Opthamology Cardiology Gastroenterology Pathology Dermatology To find out more information or to apply please contact a Health Services Specialist Recruiter: HSRecruiting-RecrutementSS@forces.gc.ca Find a Recruiting Centre Reserve Force members are trained to the same level as their Regular Force counterparts.
